explanation: The theorem is the recursion step for the library's own definition `qfact Q m := ∏ i ∈ range m, (1 - Q^(i+1))`. Its proof just unfolds that definition and applies the generic `Finset.prod_range_succ`, and generic big-operator lemmas don't count. All the mathematical content is in the library's own definition. I found no q-factorial or q-Pochhammer definition in Mathlib to compare against. A grep for qPochhammer, qFactorial, "q-Pochhammer" and "q-factorial" turned up only a TODO note in RingTheory/Polynomial/Pochhammer.lean, which lists q-factorials, q-binomials and q-Pochhammer as not yet formalized.
